title: Alcohols: oxidation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: OR15#t3 term and clue written for the game; OR15#t1 term and clue written for the game; OR15#t2 term and clue written for the game; OR15#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: OR15#N.2, OR15#N.6, OR15#N.7, OR15#N.9, OR15#N.11.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Tertiary alcohol
items.clue: Has no H on the carbon bearing the –OH, so acidified dichromate(VI) stays orange.

items.label: Aldehyde
items.clue: First product of oxidising a primary alcohol, e.g. ethanal; distilled off as it forms.

items.label: Ketone
items.clue: Product of oxidising a secondary alcohol, e.g. propanone; it cannot be oxidised further.

items.label: Reflux
items.clue: Heating with a vertical condenser, open at the top, so ethanal returns to the flask and becomes the acid.

questions.stem: Which of these is a secondary alcohol?

options.text: Butan-1-ol, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH
Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃
2-methylpropan-1-ol, (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH
2-methylbutan-2-ol, (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃

questions.explanation: The C–OH carbon is bonded to two other carbons (CH₃ and CH₂CH₃), so the alcohol is secondary.

questions.stem: Propan-1-ol is heated with an acidified oxidising agent in apparatus set up for distillation, and the distillate is collected. What is the main organic product collected, and why?

options.text: Propanoic acid, as distillation keeps propanal in the flask
Propanone, as the alcohol is oxidised to a ketone
Propanal, as it distils out before it can be oxidised further
Propanoic acid, as it forms directly in one step

questions.explanation: Propanal, CH₃CH₂CHO, is more volatile than the alcohol and the acid. It leaves the flask as vapour before it can be oxidised to propanoic acid.

questions.stem: Pentan-3-ol is heated under reflux with excess acidified potassium dichromate(VI). Which equation is correct?

options.text: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ + 2[O] → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂COOH + H₂O
CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ + [O] → CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂CHO + H₂O
No reaction, since the C–OH carbon carries no hydrogen atom.
CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ + [O] → CH₃CH₂COCH₂CH₃ + H₂O

questions.explanation: Pentan-3-ol is a secondary alcohol, so it gives a ketone, pentan-3-one, and oxidation stops there.

questions.stem: Three colourless liquids, X, Y and Z, are butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol, in some order. Each is warmed with acidified potassium dichromate(VI). X and Y turn the mixture green; Z leaves it orange. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: Z is 2-methylpropan-2-ol, the tertiary alcohol.
Z is butan-1-ol, as primary alcohols are oxidised only under reflux.
X and Y are both primary, as only primary alcohols turn the dichromate green.
The test shows that X is butan-1-ol and Y is butan-2-ol.

questions.explanation: Its C–OH carbon carries no H, so it is not oxidised and the dichromate stays orange.

questions.stem: A few drops of cyclohexanol, a six-carbon ring with an –OH on one ring carbon, are warmed with acidified potassium dichromate(VI). What do you see, and why?

options.text: It stays orange, as an –OH on a ring carbon makes the alcohol tertiary.
Orange to green: it is oxidised to cyclohexanone as Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced to Cr³⁺.
Orange to green: it is oxidised to a carboxylic acid with six carbons, as Cr₂O₇²⁻ is reduced.
Orange to green: it is reduced to cyclohexane, while the dichromate(VI) ions are oxidised.

questions.explanation: Secondary alcohol → ketone. The alcohol loses the H from O–H and the H from the C–OH carbon. Dichromate(VI), orange, is reduced to green Cr³⁺.
